title: LENDING LEDGER AND SAVING CIRCLE
body: Project proposal and revised prototype
Java 21 desktop application for lending records and shared savings
note: Records only. Money and belongings are exchanged outside the system.

title: INTRODUCTION
body: A shared record of money loans, borrowed belongings and group savings.
Both loan parties confirm the terms, handover and repayment or return.
The desktop app supports multiple signed-in account tabs on one computer.
Saving circles keep contributions and spending separate from loan balances.
note: Current implementation: Swing interface, Spring services, JDBC and embedded H2.

title: CONCEPT DESCRIPTION
body: Lending ledger: versioned agreements, confirmed handovers, partial repayments and item returns.
Reminders: due-soon, due-today and overdue notices while the app is running.
Return reliability: on-time completed borrowing records / completed borrowing records.
Saving circles: goals, schedules, invitations, contribution review and retained history.

title: THE PROBLEM
body: Loan details get lost across messages and memory.
A repayment claim needs review before it changes the balance.
Groups need consent before membership and a clear contribution approval process.
Late review should not rewrite when an exchange or submission happened.
note: Goal: shared records with explicit confirmation and clear dates.

title: SCOPE AND LIMITATIONS
body: Included: accounts, lending and borrowing tabs, receipts for loan activities, notices and calendar export.
Included: circle goals, schedules, invitations, contribution review and leaving with history retained.
Excluded: payment processing, bank/e-wallet integration and automatic proof of real-world exchanges.
Local prototype: account tabs share one database; this is not a remote multi-device service.
note: Loan reliability is not a credit score. No circle contribution score is currently calculated.

title: SIGNIFICANCE OF THE STUDY
body: Lenders and borrowers: review agreed dates and confirmed remaining balances.
Members: accept invitations and submit their own contributions for review.
Organisers: approve or reject contributions and reconcile the recorded balance.
Student groups: track borrowed equipment and shared project savings.
Project team: apply Java desktop design, transactions, validation and relational modelling.

title: DEFINITION OF TERMS
body: Actual date: reported date of the external handover, payment or return.
Submission time: when the record was created in the system.
Review time: when another party approved, confirmed or rejected the record.
Recorded circle balance: approved contributions minus approved expenses and withdrawals.
Return reliability: loan completion punctuality; no completed history means Not yet rated.

title: USER EXPERIENCE: ACCOUNT TABS
body: Create an account, then sign in through the desktop window.
New account tab lets another registered user sign in on the same computer.
Navigation: Overview, Lending ledger, Borrowing, Savings pools, Reminders & trust.
Saved actions refresh the open account tabs; notices refresh every five seconds.
note: Updated description of the desktop UI; the old browser login mockup no longer represents the implementation.

title: USER EXPERIENCE: LENDING
body: Agreement: review parties, terms version, dates and acknowledgements.
Handover: lender records the exchange; borrower reviews it before activation.
Repayment / item return: borrower submits; lender confirms or disputes.
Receipts: attached to loan activities, not automatic payment verification.
Overview: outstanding balances and loan return reliability.
note: Circle membership and savings do not change the loan return reliability percentage.

title: USER EXPERIENCE: SAVINGS POOLS
body: Invitations: accept or decline before becoming a member.
Members: submit own contribution, date and note; see Pending review in entry history.
Organiser: select an entry, approve it or reject with a reason.
Balance and goal progress include approved entries only.
Leave circle: keeps history read-only; withdraw own pending entries or wait for review before leaving.
note: Organiser records expenses/withdrawals and may close the circle; closing is blocked while reviews remain.

title: SOFTWARE REQUIREMENTS
body: Platform: Java 21 Swing desktop application; no browser or HTTP server required.
Application services: Spring Boot with WebApplicationType.NONE.
Persistence: Spring JDBC / JdbcTemplate and an embedded H2 file database.
Security: BCrypt password hashing and service-level actor checks.
Build: Maven; IDE: NetBeans or IntelliJ IDEA. Packaged executable JAR supplied.
note: Replaces the obsolete Spring MVC, Thymeleaf and JPA stack listed in the original proposal.

title: HARDWARE AND DEMONSTRATION
body: A desktop or laptop capable of running Java 21 and the Swing interface.
A writable project folder for data/lendly.mv.db and application files.
Planning target: 8 GB RAM and 5 GB free storage for development tools.
Offline classroom demo: one computer, several account tabs, one local database.
Remote accounts on different computers require a future server/shared-data architecture.
note: Planning targets are not measured minimum requirements. Back up the database with the app closed.

title: PROJECT ROLES
body: Project manager: scope, schedule and documentation.
UI/UX designer: desktop forms, feedback and invitation/review flows.
Developer: service checks, transactions, schema migration and Swing actions.
Data administrator: backups, access rules and retained ledger records.
QA: invitation consent, approval, rejection, leaving and date-preservation tests.

title: NEW FEATURE: LEAVING A CIRCLE
body: A member explicitly confirms Leave circle.
Pending contributions must be reviewed or withdrawn by the member before leaving.
Membership becomes LEFT; member and ledger rows are not deleted.
The former member keeps a read-only view of shared history and stops receiving contribution reminders.
The organiser closes the circle instead of leaving; no automatic refund is created.
note: Any settlement or payout occurs outside the app and must be recorded separately by the organiser.

title: DATES, APPROVAL AND FAIRNESS
body: Actual date records the reported exchange date; submission time is system-recorded.
Review time is separate. Approving later does not replace either original date.
A pending contribution has no effect on the approved balance.
The existing loan return score is unchanged by circle contributions or approval delay.
Future circle punctuality: count timely submissions only after approval, and assign a scheduled period explicitly.
note: Example: due Nov 24, submitted Nov 24, approved Nov 27. Submission remains Nov 24; approval delay is not member lateness.

title: SUGGESTED NEXT FEATURES
body: Contribution-period selector: assign each approved amount to a specific due date, including partial amounts.
Review reminders: tell the organiser how many contributions await review and how old they are.
Corrections: link a replacement submission to the rejected original without deleting the audit history.
Receipt export: let both parties export a shared circle statement for reconciliation.
note: Suggestions only; these are not claimed as implemented in this revision.
